title: WATERLINE: Is Sasquatch thinking about you, too?
excerpt: I’ve been around long enough to know there are things I don’t — and never will — know.
content:
I’ve been around long enough to know there are things I don’t — and never will — know.

So when my kid asked me if I believe in ghosts, UFOs or good songs by the band KISS, I had a fairly standard answer.

“Not really, but I also know most things are possible.”

Clearly, some things are more likely than others. Like, aliens could land their spacecraft on my lawn and demand I tell them a good song by KISS, and I’ll have to tell them such a thing likely doesn’t exist.

Or a swamp ape could show up and play a drum and, by default, perform a better tune than that band.

Not really sure why I’m dogging on KISS right now. Just kinda happening.

What I am trying to write about is the faith that things exist we won’t know about — and that’s OK.

A friend of mine went camping in the Northwest recently and overheard a discussion between sober individuals discussing Bigfoot. A woman who lived in this very rural area said without hesitation nor fear of mocking that she’d seen Sasquatch twice in her life.

When I was in Alaska a few months ago, the thought crossed my mind as we traveled north from Juneau to Denali. I squinted a few times into the tree line. I did not see a Sasquatch, but I was on a loud train so he/she/they likely had a chance to duck down into a brush area while I passed.

There is a funny reoccurring theme in a few episodes of “The Newsroom” when a young staffer is trying to convince a mainstream news anchor that it was worth their time to do a report on cryptozoology ... the study of creatures not yet known.

The deeper we went into the water, the more we realized sea life doesn’t care too much about cold, dark, water pressure or nutrition. For some reason, that reminds me of my fourth ex-wife.

Anyway, as we have explored the world, we have found critters through microscopes, extreme submersibles and among the highest trees. Sometimes it’s a fungus or fish; sometimes a bird ever-so-slightly different than others.

And while Flock cameras will definitely catch Sasquatch sooner or later as he does some Constitutionally protected activity like protesting or assembling, it hasn’t yet.

There was once an overnight radio show that would talk all sorts of crazy. I listened to it all the time. Also, I lived weird hours. Also, it’s addicting to listen to all sorts of crazy — if you’re not 100% crazy.

So Art Bell would talk chupacabra, some sort of dog/cat/inner-dimensional creature that was causing chaos in Spanish-speaking countries ... ripping up lifestock in awful ways. It was slightly more believable than Bat Boy (not the baseball position), but still seemed unlikely.

Unlikely is not impossible.

So are there angels, demons; Sith lords (just two); swamp apes; toddlers not dripping germs constantly; or evil geniuses who are having second thoughts on how artificial intelligence is being used? It’s plausible.

But let’s not spend too much time thinking about it.

Sasquatch is not thinking too much about you.

Or maybe Sasquatch is...
